extracted.intended_audience: SBIR grant reviewers and diagnostic assay developers (MBio team / regulatory reviewers)
extracted.subtask_description: Design, integrate, validate, and pre-market evaluate a portable, CLIA-waivable rapid HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody combination assay (cartridge + reader + on-cartridge reagents) to performance equivalent to FDA-approved 4th generation laboratory assays. Includes assay optimization, cartridge/fluidic design, reagent lyophilization, validation panels, human subjects protections, and pre-market usability testing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meet FDA CLIA waiver guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2 milestone: a portable, integrated system delivered to clinical collaborators that meets FDA CLIA waiver guidance requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accomplished through cartridge design modifications, on-cartridge lyophilization of reagents, minimization of user steps (target: two user interventions), automated wash integration if necessary, and validation/field testing in intended-use settings prior to pre-IDE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assay performance equivalence to 4th gen lab assays
rubrics_metrics.description: The Aim 1 and Aim 3 milestones are an HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody detection assay/system with performance equivalent to FDA-approved laboratory 4th gen Ag/Ab combo assays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the FDA-approved Bio-Rad GS HIV Combo Ag/Ab EIA as the reference test; test with specified commercial performance panels and clinical specimens; aim for ~95% sensitivity and specificity (sample sizes chosen give 95% CI ±3%).

rubrics_metrics.name: p24 detection sensitivity/specificity analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze p24 detection sensitivity and specificity with a three-point titration of the NIBSC p24 standard and an 8-member HIV-negative serum panel (four non-heterophilic antibody samples and four known HA-containing samples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform iterative screening; titration results of labeled detect Ab inform dye choice and conjugation strategy (e.g., A647 vs SLP3); validate with Phase I collection controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody-dye conjugation and print optimization metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Optimize antibody-dye conjugation and Ab print buffers using a Design of Experiments (DOE) approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary metrics: spot signal/noise, morphology (intra-spot %CV), and lot-to-lot reproducibility. Use dye-labeled recombinant p24 and anti-species Ab as fluorescent probes and follow a protocol that mimics current HIV-1 Ab assay steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: p24 monoclonal antibody (mAb) pair selection criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a high-affinity anti-p24 monoclonal antibody sandwich pair, testing additional candidate antibodies as both detection and capture agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include availability of long-term supply agreements as part of mAb evaluation; test candidates iteratively and evaluate conjugation compatibility and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: HIV-1 and HIV-2 antigen selection and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Test alternative HIV-1 and HIV-2 antigens (including recombinant proteins and antigenic peptides) to improve performance and ensure multiple reliable reagent sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure assay sensitivity/specificity with anti-HIV-1/2 combo performance panel (SeraCare # PRZ207); investigate non-specific binding between candidate capture antigens and the anti-p24 detect mAb (and vice versa); incorporate print buffer optimization and label detect antigens with A647 or equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimize detect antigen concentration to avoid saturation and hook effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Titrate the stoichiometry of labeled detect antigen relative to sample target antibody to balance sensitivity across low- and high-titer samples.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In low-titer samples, high detect Ag concentration can prevent bridging (reducing sensitivity); in very high titer samples, low detect Ag can result in captured antibodies unbound to detect Ag (hook effect). Use panels of very high and very low titer samples to finalize concentrations; Phase I data suggest a two-fold reduction could improve low-titer signal without sacrificing high-titer detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop virus disruption sample additive (VDSA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop a detergent-based virus disruption reagent to improve p24 immunoassay sensitivity while not adversely affecting the serology component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optimize VDSA performance and develop lyophilized, heat-stable formulations for on-cartridge use; reagent lyophilization is further addressed under Aim 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combine antibody and antigen detection with attention to cross-reactivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate HIV-1/2 Ab detection and p24 Ag detection reagents within a single array/sample additive while minimizing cross-reactivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust sample additive and wash buffer formulations as needed; target a mutually effective incubation time between 10–20 minutes; assess whether a post-incubation wash (single wash) is required to meet performance goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leverage planar waveguide excitation to reduce background signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploit planar waveguide technology so that only fluorescent molecules on or very near the waveguide surface are excited, minimizing free-fluor in-solution background.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This physical property supports a simple protocol (short incubation, minimal wash) and contributes to observed whole blood assay performance, but a wash may still boost performance if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimal assay protocol steps and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a minimal user protocol: (1) add sample to cartridge entrance port; (2) incubate 10–20 minutes; (3) insert cartridge into reader and receive results 15–30 seconds later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design assay flow and incubation to meet CLIA-waiver simplicity goals; allow for an optional automated post-incubation wash if needed to meet assay performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use specified performance and challenge panels for method development
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate assay with multiple commercial seroconversion/performance panels and an expanded 80-sample 'challenge panel' from UCSD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels listed: SeraCare PRB109 and PRB965; ZeptoMetrix 9075, 9079, 12008; SeraCare PRZ207 and PRZ208; SeraCare PRF203 (HIV-2); plus 80-sample challenge panel characterized by NAT and Abbott ARCHITECT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation sample size and composition for Aim 3
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate system with a panel of ≥200 HIV-positive specimens (including minimum 20 acute infection samples) and 200 HIV-negative samples for specificity testing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive panel to include acute (RNA+/Ab-), early seroconversion (WB indeterminate), seropositive (HIV-1 & HIV-2), high-titer samples, commercially available subtype panels, and incidence/prevalence panels. With assumed 95% sensitivity and specificity, these sample numbers provide 95% confidence intervals of ±3%.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test potentially interfering substances at specified thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether lipemic, icteric, hemolyzed, and proteinemic samples affect assay performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test thresholds: lipemic samples ≥ 1000 mg/dL triglycerides; icteric samples ≥ 20 mg/dL bilirubin; hemolyzed samples ≥ 500 mg/dL hemoglobin; proteinemic samples ≥ 12 g/dL protein.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cartridge fluidic channel geometry optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Alter cartridge channel geometry to reduce volume and flow rate to improve analyte on-rate and diffusion binding to printed proteins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test channel widths of 2 mm and heights of 0.145, 0.1, 0.075 and 0.050 mm (note: text lists 0.50 mm but intent is to test multiple heights), evaluate time-to-fill, flow rate, and fraction of sample over printed proteins; changes can be made by altering die-cut adhesive gasket dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample loading robustness and fingerstick compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Design inlet port to accept finger stick whole blood directly (no transfer pipets required) via capillary fill; also compatible with transfer devices for venous blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target assay precision across sample volume range of 10 to 30 μL; current cartridge covers with ~18 μL; redesign aims to reduce required volume to ≤10 μL.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-cartridge internal quality controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Integrate on-cartridge controls to confirm proper sample introduction and reagent formulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Add anti-detect reagent antibodies downstream of capture reagents (e.g., anti-mouse IgG Ab, anti-gp41 Ab, anti-gp36 Ab) to serve as reagent formulation controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-board dried reagent performance requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: On-cartridge dried (lyophilized) reagents must be heat-stable, rapidly hydrate, and disperse evenly throughout the sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Study excipients and caking agents to ensure rapid reconstitution; ensure sample volume contacting lyophilized reagent is controlled via cartridge hydrodynamics (channel geometry, surface energy, capillary gates); seal cartridges in vapor-barrier pouches with desiccant and perform real-time and accelerated stability testing in temperature/humidity-controlled chambers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Automated wash buffer delivery option
rubrics_metrics.description: If a post-incubation wash is required to meet performance, develop an approach to deliver wash buffer without user intervention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One approach: place a blister pack above a reservoir/channel directing wash buffer to the assay channel, released by a simple solenoid-driven plunger in the instrument. If unsuccessful, alternative is manual addition of wash buffer to entrance port (requires intervention but minimal metering).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two user-intervention design goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim 2 expected outcome: an assay system that delivers results with only two user intervention steps—sample addition and cartridge insertion into reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design tradeoffs and cartridge features should prioritize meeting this simplicity objective to support CLIA waivers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risks and mitigation strategies for lyophilized reagents
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary risk: reconstitution of lyophilized reagents may be too slow or non-reproducible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives: modify cartridge to further restrict sample flow (improve reconstitution control), test alternative caking reagents and lyophilization protocols, or implement alternative wash delivery methods if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-market evaluation objectives and sample plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Place systems in intended-use settings to capture operational/usability feedback and generate a preliminary dataset on capillary whole blood samples from ~100 study participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct at UCSD HIV care clinics under subaward co-investigators; study goals: (1) generate usability dataset, (2) establish performance in intended use setting; donors provide finger stick and venous samples; collect both usability and performance data to support pre-IDE meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability testing and human factors standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Human factors analysis and usability testing will follow FDA and ISO 13485 guidance and will include surveys and direct observation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate human factors into MBio's Quality Management System; include as part of Design and Risk Management Processes; results inform product design lock and pre-IDE discussions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intended-use performance and reproducibility checks
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess sensitivity relative to FDA approved rapid tests and Bio-Rad GS Combo, and establish reproducibility of system by running venous samples in triplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish accuracy and precision of finger stick samples relative to venous samples and evaluate operational performance in clinic workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and safety monitoring procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Monitor data and safety at institutional and project levels, report adverse events according to institutional policy, and include NIH project officers in monitoring plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor occurrences of adverse events associated with specimen/data collection; maintain data integrity through conference calls and face-to-face meetings; report events to study team and institution as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: All human subjects research will comply with 45 CFR 46 and OHRP guidance for repositories; clinical sites must hold a Federal Wide Assurance (FWA) and obtain IRB/Ethics approval before implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key personnel must complete NIH-recognized human subjects protection training; certifications kept on file; no research without local IRB approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment, informed consent, and documentation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Recruitment and consent will follow IRB-approved procedures, include written informed consent translated/back-translated as needed, and documentation maintained in participant records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete descriptive information including risks, alternatives, compensation; consent process documented in study chart; additional IRB-approved educational/recruitment materials provided as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for confidentiality and specimen/data handling
rubrics_metrics.description: De-identify data submitted to project database using patient-specific ID (PID); master linkage between PID and identifiers accessible only to local study personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aliquoted specimens may be retained at study sites for supporting studies; future use of stored specimens allowed only after review/approval and confirmation coverage by existing informed consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion and exclusion criteria for participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Enroll adults (>18) at risk for or tested for HIV who can provide informed consent; exclude vulnerable populations such as prisoners and children (children may be included in later phases); pregnant women may participate if consenting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility, inclusion, and exclusion criteria will be detailed in specific protocols; children excluded due to inability to provide independent consent and sample quality concerns for this phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation of women and minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Women and minorities will be appropriately represented in recruitment reflective of local HIV epidemiology; distribution by sex will reflect local statistics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explore any sex- or race/ethnicity-based differences in secondary analyses where enrollment allows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential risks, benefits, and participant safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate minimal physical risk (venipuncture), potential psychological/social risks (stigma) and document measures to limit harms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform participants of alternatives and risks in consent; maintain confidentiality; provide clinical care discretion to primary physicians; mitigate psychological impact and report adverse events per protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned enrollment and demographic reporting consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned enrollment table lists target totals by ethnic and racial categories that must be internally consistent (Ethnic Category total must equal Racial Categories total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example planned enrollment: total 100 participants with specified breakdowns (Hispanic/Non-Hispanic and race categories); ensure tabular totals match as required by reporting format.
